label: Whole-suffix completeness and universal law projection
term: whole-suffix completeness and universal law projection
definition: SuffixComplete p n means that, after the fixed observed true prefix through n, EVERY entire Boolean future suffix is admitted by Cell p on n. UniversalProjection p q n means that the same supplied Profile q is satisfied by every admitted whole trace, rather than only a selected actual trace. A future-excluding q forbids some state transition at time t >= n+1; deterministic q admits at most one successor at each time and current state. Separately, scheduled switches supplies one deterministic copy-or-toggle profile for each complete switch schedule, and scheduleOf f extracts a schedule from the complete f retrospectively. None of these conditions supplies actuality, metaphysical accessibility, independent governing efficacy, physical identity of a bearer, or an adequate explanation of why a selected law obtains.
note: Analyst construction tied to existing #737 Profile/Cell, #743 UsesRecord, and #736 extensional whole-history distinction. A simple example is a fixed record of a switch staying on through n with any later Boolean states allowed. A counterexample is the stable copy Profile: after its initial true state, a false successor is disallowed. A law banning one future transition cannot project universally across a suffix-complete alternative class. No real-world unrestricted modal range is asserted: the specific bridge from absence of ultimate grounding to this strong condition is OPEN. Another counterexample to that bridge is the existing ungrounded `brute` totality scope paired with a stable law; its independence is structural only. The schedule-of-path construction is ex post and may be a target copy, not an independent explanation. Source comparison and actual metaphysical application remain unresolved; see docs/notes/no-foundation-law-chaos.md.
